26/G.goal: Explain the perceptual and proprioceptive processes that shape XR experience and how sensory mismatches can cause cybersickness or presence loss.
26/G.achieves: Provides the human-factor foundation needed in the course to understand XR sensory systems and to evaluate or design XR experiences with reduced discomfort and greater presence.

26/O1.goal: Explain the human perceptual process by which sensory signals are received, neurally transmitted, hierarchically processed, and combined with memory to form interpreted perception.
26/O1.achieves: Equips the learner to interpret later course material on XR visual, auditory, and other sensory systems by establishing how raw sensory input becomes perceived experience.

26/O2.goal: Explain how proprioception contributes to body-aware perception and how sensory conflicts in XR can cause cybersickness or presence loss, including design implications from vection.
26/O2.achieves: Enables the learner to connect human bodily perception to XR comfort issues and to recognize design constraints for reducing cybersickness and supporting presence.
